items.title: Show HN: Hop – project sessions beyond tmux
items.contentSnippet:
hop started from a frustration: every project I work on accumulates browser tabs, while tmux sessions can only contain terminals. This really started getting out of hand once coding agents took hold, as more things are now going on at the same time.
On top of that, I've started doing more work in sandboxed environments, and tmux isn't great at managing sessions across different environments - it wants a tmux server everywhere.
So hop moves the project session up to the window-manager level: term

items.title: Show HN: I Built a CLI for Proton Mail, Drive, Calendar, Pass and Contacts
items.contentSnippet:
I made a command line tool for Proton. It covers Mail, Drive, Calendar, Pass and Contacts. It is one static binary for Linux, macOS and Windows.
Proton doesn't have a CLI for all their web interfaces. There is one for Drive and one for Pass, but the other ones are not really there. There's no Mail CLI, Contacts or other CLIs. I wanted to have everything in one.

items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN, I’m Lewis, a student building InterviewsRadar as a side project.
I built it to help people find someone who recently interviewed for a specific company and role, and have a conversation about the experience.
You can post an experience you’re willing to share, or a request for something you’re looking for. Conversations can cover the interview process, preparation, and lessons learned.

items.title: Show HN: Analyst Index – analysts who make money telling you good stock calls
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN!
What if analyst ratings could be relied on to help you find the next Sandisk, before it takes off?
On Analyst Index, analysts publish price targets with a maturity date. Every call gets scored against what the stock actually did, so an analyst builds a record on accuracy instead of on follower count.
